newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bushfire season starts in earnest.
newsitem.headline: Australia bushfire season starts in earnest.

text.p: Australia's bushfire season has arrived with more than 100 fires in three states destroying tens of thousands of hectares (acres) during the past two days, fire officials said on Monday.
About 4,000 firefighters were on standby in Queensland as extremely hot weather and gusty winds are expected to fan bushfires in the southeast of the state.

"It could be a hellish day if the weather predictions for today are correct but overall, things are not looking too bad at this stage," said Alan Gillespie, fire inspector for southeast Queensland. "It's a waiting game at this stage."

The fire causing the main concern was near Chinchilla, 160 km (99 miles) northwest of Brisbane, where 5,000 hectares (12,355 acres) had been burnt. Other fires were only 30 km (19 miles) from the state capital Brisbane.

In the state of South Australia fire fighters were battling to control some 80 fires, most in remote bush and pastoral land. The largest fire, sparked by a lightning strike, had burnt 20,000 hectares (49,420 acres) of the Flinders Range. In New South Wales 12 fires were burning out of control in the northeast of the state.
Fire officials in the three states said the fires had not damaged any urban areas or caused any injuries.
Total fire bans have been imposed in the three states with temperatures forecast to range between the high 30s and 40 degrees Celsius (86-104 Fahrenheit), with winds gusting up to 60 kmh (37 mph).
In January 1994 hundreds of bushfires raged across eastern Australia, with fires ringing the harbour city of Sydney, dropping ash on beaches, burning homes and killing four people.

Australia's bushfire seasons normally runs during the summer months of December to February, but can be longer as the island continent often suffers severe droughts leaving much of the country tinder-dry.
